% T9, C2 on the synthetic JSON probe.  commit 813e093c6c4972c54ec021a5d410b55df0a21a09
% Main variant ft110m-v3-visible by the pre-set rule (artifacts/probe/main_variant.json); Alt = ft110m-v3; Untuned = untuned-v3.
% Sources: artifacts/probe/results/grid_<tag>.json, rho_check_<tag>.json, val_rescored.json, history_<tag>.jsonl.
%
% Grid cells: \CTwo[Alt|Untuned]<Rule><Q>at<Rho><K>[Lo|Hi], e.g. \CTwoConfAatRhoOneKEight
%   no variant word = the main variant; Rule: Conf = confidence top-k, Rand = random positions
%   Q: A = (A) dependency, B = (B) estimation, nats per field (mean over the instances at that rho);
%      ShareA = (A) as a percentage of (A)+(B)
%   Rho: RhoZero, RhoQuarter, RhoHalf, RhoThreeQuarters, RhoOne;  K: KOne, KTwo, KFour, KEight
%   Lo/Hi (main variant only): 95% bootstrap interval, instances resampled
% Crossover: \CTwo[Alt|Untuned]<Rule>CrossKat<Rho> = the first k at which mean (A) > mean (B);
%   ...CrossKCIat<Rho> = the first k at which the 95% interval of (A)-(B) is above 0;
%   -- = at no k <= 8.  ...CrossRhoMin = the smallest rho with a crossover, ...ShareAMax = the largest ShareA.
%
% ft110m-v3-visible (main variant): 1000 instances, 10000 resamples

%   \CTwoTTen[Llada]<Q>K<K>[Lo|Hi]   Q: Dis = disagreement (fraction of the k committed
%   positions where parallel and sequential tokens differ; 0 at k = 1 by construction),
%   Delta = conf - agree (positive = overconfident), CE = -log p(true token) in nats;
%   K: KOne, KTwo, KFour, KEight; Lo/Hi: 95% document-bootstrap interval
% All ten rates, including the shared all-[MASK] state at rate 1.0 (per_k):
%   \CTwoTTen[Llada]<Q>AllRatesK<K>[Lo|Hi]
% Disagreement per k and mask rate (per_k_rate): \CTwoTTen[Llada]DisK<K>Rate<R>[Lo|Hi],
%   R: PtOne ... PtNine = 0.1 ... 0.9, One = 1.0;  ...DisMaxUpToRatePtSeven = the largest
%   disagreement over k and the rates up to 0.7
% Contrasts between k, over all ten rates (contrasts): \CTwoTTen[Llada]Contrast<Name>[Lo|Hi]
% Probe (110M only): no variant word = ft110m-v3-visible (T9's main variant), Alt = ft110m-v3;
%   ...ProbeSpearman[Lo|Hi] = Spearman of disagreement with the exact (A) per field over the

\setbeamersize{text margin left=8mm,text margin right=8mm}

\setbeamerfont{framesubtitle}{size=\small,series=\mdseries}

\makeatletter
\setbeamertemplate{frametitle}{%
  \vspace*{4mm}%
  {\usebeamerfont{frametitle}\usebeamercolor[fg]{frametitle}\insertframetitle\par}%
  \ifx\insertframesubtitle\@empty\else
    {\vspace{0.6mm}\usebeamerfont{framesubtitle}\color{ink2}\insertframesubtitle\par}%

}
\makeatother

\setbeamertemplate{itemize/enumerate subbody begin}{\setlength{\itemsep}{1pt}}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
\newcommand{\pp}{\,pp\xspace}

\newcommand{\ci}[1]{{\color{ink2}\scriptsize[#1]}}
\newcommand{\fnote}[1]{{\color{ink2}\scriptsize #1\par}}
\newcommand{\lbl}[1]{{\color{accentdark}\firasemibold #1}}

\newcommand{\B}{{\color{est}\firasemibold (B)}\xspace}

\newcolumntype{R}{>{\raggedleft\arraybackslash}X}

  arc=1.2mm, left=3mm, right=3mm, top=1.2mm, bottom=1.2mm,
  borderline west={1.6pt}{0pt}{accent}, fontupper=\small,
  before upper=\raggedright, #1}

\newtcolorbox{panel}[1][]{enhanced, colback=white, colframe=base, boxrule=0.5pt,
  arc=1.2mm, left=2.4mm, right=2.4mm, top=1.4mm, bottom=1.4mm, fontupper=\footnotesize,
  before upper=\raggedright, #1}

\newcommand{\paneltitle}[1]{{\color{accentdark}\small\firasemibold #1}\par\vspace{0.8mm}}

% placeholder for results that arrive after pass 1: {when}{what produces them}
\newtcolorbox{pending}[3][]{enhanced, colback=wash, frame hidden, arc=1.2mm,
  borderline={0.9pt}{0pt}{accent, dash pattern=on 3pt off 2pt},
  left=3mm, right=3mm, top=2mm, bottom=2mm, fontupper=\small, before upper={\raggedright
    {\color{accentdark}\fontsize{11}{13}\selectfont\firasemibold RESULTS LAND #2}\par
    \vspace{0.6mm}{\color{ink2}\footnotesize #3}\par\vspace{1.6mm}}, #1}

\newcommand{\CresCI}[1]{$\Cres{#1}$\;\ci{$\Cres{#1Lo},\,\Cres{#1Hi}$}}

% symbol #2 if the interval [#1Lo, #1Hi] excludes 0
\newcommand{\Cexcl}[2]{\Cyesfalse\ifcsname #1Lo\endcsname\ifcsname #1Hi\endcsname
  \ifnum\fpeval{(\csname #1Lo\endcsname>0)||(\csname #1Hi\endcsname<0)}=1 \Cyestrue\fi\fi\fi\ifCyes #2\fi}
% one arm of the claim table: {display name}{label}
\newcommand{\CClaimRow}[2]{#1
  & \Cnum{COne#2ContrastUni} & \Cnum{COne#2ContrastDecTopkConfKFour}
  & \Cnum{COneFieldContrast#2Uni} & \Cnum{COneFieldContrast#2DecTopkConfKFour} \\}
% one arm of the beta_z table
\newcommand{\CBetaRow}[2]{#1
  & \Cnum{COne#2BetaZNoFEUni} & \Cnum{COne#2BetaZNoFEDecTopkConfKFour}
  & \Cnum{COne#2BetaZFEUni} & \Cnum{COne#2BetaZFEDecTopkConfKFour} \\}
% T8 cell: with-control value and a double dagger if the paired difference excludes 0
\newcommand{\CTEight}[2]{\Cnum{#1With}$^{\Cexcl{#1Difference}{\ddagger}}$}

% natural size, scaled down (never up) to fit {width}{height}
\newsavebox{\fitbin}
\newcommand{\fitbox}[3]{%
  \sbox{\fitbin}{#3}%
  \edef\fitscale{\fpeval{min(1, \number\dimexpr#1\relax/\number\wd\fitbin, \number\dimexpr#2\relax/\number\dimexpr\ht\fitbin+\dp\fitbin\relax)}}%
  \ifdim\fitscale pt<1pt\scalebox{\fitscale}{\usebox{\fitbin}}\else\usebox{\fitbin}\fi}

% pending box with the final height: {height}{when}{what is missing}{what it will show}
\newcommand{\Pend}[4]{\begin{pending}[height from=#1 to 90mm]{#2}{#3}\small #4\end{pending}}

% ================================================================ 2 motivation 
\begin{frame}{Diffusion LMs write by filling in blanks, surest first}
  \framesubtitle{Each step the model guesses every blank at once and keeps the $k$ guesses it is surest of}
  \vspace{0.5mm}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.56\textwidth}
      \centering
      % illustrative toy, not data
      \begin{tikzpicture}[x=0.98cm, y=0.8cm,
          tok/.style={draw=base, line width=0.5pt, rounded corners=1.5pt,
            minimum width=0.86cm, minimum height=0.52cm, inner sep=0pt, font=\footnotesize},
          obs/.style={tok, fill=plane, text=ink},
          msk/.style={tok, fill=white, text=muted},
          win/.style={tok, fill=wash, draw=accent, line width=0.8pt, text=ink}]
        \node[obs] at (1,2.7) {The};
        \node[win] at (2,2.7) {[M]};
        \node[msk] at (3,2.7) {[M]};
        \node[obs] at (4,2.7) {on};
        \node[win] at (5,2.7) {[M]};
        \node[msk] at (6,2.7) {[M]};
        \node[msk] at (7,2.7) {[M]};
        \node[obs] at (8,2.7) {.};
        \foreach \x in {2,5} \node[font=\scriptsize\firasemibold, text=accentdark] at (\x,3.24) {commit};
        \draw[base, line width=0.5pt] (0.5,0) -- (8.5,0);
        \foreach \x/\c/\w/\col in {2/0.91/cat/accent, 3/0.42/sat/base, 5/0.97/the/accent,
                                   6/0.30/red/base, 7/0.77/mat/base} {
          \fill[\col] (\x-0.17,0) rectangle (\x+0.17,{1.85*\c});
          \node[font=\scriptsize, text=ink] at (\x,{1.85*\c+0.17}) {\c};
          \node[font=\footnotesize\itshape, text=ink2] at (\x,-0.25) {\w};
        }
        \node[font=\scriptsize, text=muted, anchor=west] at (0.4,-0.68)
          {bar: confidence $c_i$ of the best guess per blank; the top $k = 2$ are kept};
      \end{tikzpicture}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.41\textwidth}
      \begin{itemize}
        \item The model starts from all-blank text and fills it in over a few steps.
        \item Top-$k$ (LLaDA-8B, Dream-7B) keeps the $k$ surest guesses; Fast-dLLM keeps
              all guesses above a threshold.
        \item A kept token \alert{won} a contest of noisy scores: the setting of the
              \alert{winner's curse}.
      \end{itemize}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  \vspace{2mm}
  \begin{takeaway}
    \textbf{Question.} When the model is 90\% sure of a token it chose, is that token right 90\%
    of the time? And when it fills several blanks in one step, which kind of error dominates?
  \end{takeaway}
\end{frame}

% ================================================================ 3 two error sources
\begin{frame}{Filling several blanks in one step can go wrong in two ways}
  \framesubtitle{Total error of a set $S$ of tokens committed together, given the visible text}
  \vspace{-2.5mm}
  \[
    \mathrm{KL}\Big(p^{*} \,\Big\|\, \prod_{i\in S} p_{\theta,i}\Big)
    \;=\; \underbrace{\mathrm{TC}(x_S \mid x_{\mathrm{obs}})}_{\text{(A) dependency}}
    \;+\; \underbrace{\sum_{i\in S} \mathrm{KL}\big(p^{*}_i \,\big\|\, p_{\theta,i}\big)}_{\text{(B) estimation}}
  \]
  \vspace{-1mm}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.4\textwidth}
      \begin{itemize}
        \item \A Dependency: blanks are guessed separately, so the guesses can clash,
              e.g.\ \emph{New} + \emph{Angeles}.
        \item \B Estimation: each blank's own probabilities are wrong. Work on dependency
              in parallel decoding treats \B as fixed.
        \item C2 measures both where $p^{*}$ is known; C1 asks whether chosen tokens are
              overconfident.
      \end{itemize}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.57\textwidth}
      \scriptsize
      \renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.12}
      \arrayrulecolor{base}
      \begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}p{2.9cm} >{\centering\arraybackslash}X >{\centering\arraybackslash}X@{}}
        \toprule
        {\color{ink2}Work} & {\color{ink2}Checks confidence of chosen tokens?} & {\color{ink2}Separates (A) and (B)?} \\
        \midrule
        Fast-dLLM; OSDT             & no              & no \\
        KLASS; SWD; LESS            & no              & no \\
        PC-Sampler                  & positional only & no \\
        DAPD; DEMASK; PUNT          & no              & (A) only \\
        ParallelBench               & no              & (A) only \\
        Tang et al.\ (2026)         & no              & identifies \\
        \rowcolor{wash}
        \textbf{This work}          & \textbf{yes}    & \textbf{both} \\
        \bottomrule
      \end{tabularx}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

% ================================================================ 4 contributions
\begin{frame}{Three contributions}
  \vspace{2mm}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.315\textwidth}
      \begin{panel}[height=40mm]
        {\color{accent}\fontsize{16}{18}\selectfont\firasemibold C1}\par\vspace{0.8mm}
        \paneltitle{Are chosen tokens overconfident?}
        Is a token that \emph{won} against other blanks right less often than its confidence
        says? Tested on LLaDA-8B, Dream-7B (Base and Instruct) and our own 110M model.
      \end{panel}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.315\textwidth}
      \begin{panel}[height=40mm]
        {\color{accent}\fontsize{16}{18}\selectfont\firasemibold C2}\par\vspace{0.8mm}
        \paneltitle{How large are \A and \B?}
        Measured exactly on a synthetic JSON task where the true answer distribution is
        known. On real text, evaluated using disagreement and calibration proxies.
      \end{panel}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.315\textwidth}
      \begin{panel}[height=40mm]
        {\color{accent}\fontsize{16}{18}\selectfont\firasemibold C3}\par\vspace{0.8mm}
        \paneltitle{A corrected commit rule}
        Correct the model's confidence, then commit every token that clears a bar. No extra
        model calls. Compared with six decoders at equal speed on GSM8K (math) and MBPP (code).
      \end{panel}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Theory: when can winning make a token overconfident?}
  \framesubtitle{$s$: a text with blanks $M$; $\ell_i$: score of the guess at blank $i$; $a_i = 1$ if it is right}
  \vspace{1.5mm}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.485\textwidth}
      \begin{panel}[height=40mm]
        \paneltitle{Proposition 1 · Winning alone adds no bias}
        If each blank's score and correctness are independent of the other blanks' given $s$,
        and the contest $P$ is drawn independently of them, the winner $i$ of $P$ satisfies
        \[
          \Pr\big(a_i = 1 \mid \ell_i,\, s,\, i = \arg\max_{j\in P} \ell_j\big) = \pi(\ell_i, s).
        \]
        \fnote{A winner is right as often as any token with its score and context. So unequal
        noise across blanks cannot by itself bias winners}
      \end{panel}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.485\textwidth}
      \begin{panel}[height=40mm]
        \paneltitle{Proposition 2 · Winners' overconfidence has two parts}
        $\Delta(m)$: confidence minus accuracy of tokens that won among $m$ blanks.
        \[
          \Delta(m) =
          \underbrace{\mathbb{E}_m[\sigma(\ell) - \pi(\ell)]}_{\text{own miscalibration}}
          + \underbrace{\mathbb{E}_m[\pi(\ell) - \pi(\ell, s)]}_{\text{field term}}
        \]
        \fnote{$\pi(\ell)$: usual calibration curve; $\pi(\ell,s)$: the same curve given the
        context. The field term is nonzero only if accuracy at a given score depends on the
        context; with $m = 1$ (no contest) it is exactly 0.}
      \end{panel}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  \vspace{2.5mm}
  \begin{takeaway}
    So a \textbf{winner's curse} can come only from the field term
  \end{takeaway}
\end{frame}

% ================================================================ 6 estimands
\begin{frame}{C1}
  \framesubtitle{Gap $=$ confidence $-$ accuracy)}
  \vspace{0.5mm}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.315\textwidth}
      \begin{panel}[height=23mm]
        \paneltitle{E1 · gap of winners}
        $\Delta(m)$: average gap of tokens that won among $m$ blanks
        ($m \le \SetupPoolMax$). E1 $= \Delta(\SetupPoolMax) - \Delta(1)$.
      \end{panel}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.315\textwidth}
      \begin{panel}[height=23mm]
        \paneltitle{E2 · field term}
        The winner's-curse part of the gap (Proposition 2).
        E2 $=$ field$(\SetupPoolMax)-$field$(1)$.
      \end{panel}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.315\textwidth}
      \begin{panel}[height=23mm]
        \paneltitle{E3 · what decoders leave}
        Decoders fill easy blanks first. At equal confidence, are the blanks they leave
        right less often than random ones?
      \end{panel}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  \vspace{2.5mm}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.5\textwidth}
      \footnotesize\raggedright
      \textbf{Hypotheses.} \lbl{H1} E1 $> 0$; \lbl{H2} E2 $> 0$;
      \lbl{H3} blanks a decoder leaves are more overconfident than random ones.\par\vspace{1.5mm}
      % \textbf{When we claim an effect.} Its 95\% interval excludes zero, and it survives the Holm
      % correction for testing 14 cells at once (7 model/task pairs $\times$ random or decoder
      % blanks), run separately for E1 and E2. Repeat runs give identical numbers, so
      % run-to-run noise adds nothing.
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.47\textwidth}
      \footnotesize\raggedright
      \textbf{A cross-check by regression}: on winning tokens, predict correctness
      from the score $\ell_i$ and the rank in the contest, with and without one offset
      $\alpha_s$ per text. A winner's curse shows as a negative rank effect $\beta_z$ without
      the offsets that disappears with them.
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  \note{Declared also needs the estimate above twice the non-determinism floor; the floor is 0
  (repeats are bitwise identical), and delta_min = 0.02, fixed in advance, sets power. Regression:
  Pr(a=1) = sigma(alpha [+alpha_s] + f(l) + beta_z z_{r,m}), f a 9-knot spline fixed in advance;
  Eq. 3 uses rank dummies gamma_k in place of z.}
\end{frame}

% ================================================================ 8 T0 validation
\begin{frame}{Test on simulated data (T0)}
  \framesubtitle{Four simulated worlds with known answers}
  \centering\includegraphics[width=0.85\linewidth]{t0_scenarios}\par
  \vspace{1.5mm}\raggedright
  \begin{takeaway}
    \textbf{Why ECE is not enough.} When overconfidence depends on context, ECE (the usual
    calibration score) remains near zero, whereas E1 clearly captures the overconfidence.
  \end{takeaway}
\end{frame}

          \CClaimRow{Dream-I MBPP}{DreamInstructMbpp}

      \else
        \Pend{52mm}{}{Waits for \texttt{paper/tables/c1/macros\_c1.tex}, written by
          \texttt{scripts/c1\_paper\_outputs.py} from \texttt{results/c1/<Label>/results.json} and the Holm
          summary.}{One row per arm (seven arms): E1 and E2 point estimates in uniform and decoder
          ($k{=}4$) states. Intervals: backup.}
      \fi
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.395\textwidth}
      \footnotesize\raggedright
      \lbl{E1} positive: a token that won among \SetupPoolMax{} blanks is more overconfident
      than a random blank.\par\vspace{1mm}
      \lbl{E2} positive: part of that growth is the winner's curse itself
      (Proposition 2).\par\vspace{1.5mm}
      \begin{takeaway}[fontupper=\footnotesize]
        \ifCOneMacros
          \textbf{Claims.} With a decoder choosing,
          E1 is positive for every model; E2 is clearly above the estimator's known bias (T0)
          only for the instruction-tuned models.
        \else
          \textbf{Claims.} {\color{ink2}Pending: how many cells we claim.}
        \fi
      \end{takeaway}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  \note{Sign: positive means overconfident. H1 (E1): yes in the states a top-k decoder visits, every arm,
  all claimed. In uniform states the sign varies: negative and claimed for both base models and LLaDA-I GSM8K,
  positive for Dream-I; LLaDA-I MBPP and MDLM uniform are declared but not claimed. Sizes: |E1| at most 0.015
  for base and 110M, up to 0.26 for instruct MBPP. H2 (E2): claimed in all 14, positive in 12, but for base and
  110M below 0.005, of the order of what the estimator reads with no field term in T0, so we do not read it as a
  winner's curse there. Seven of eight instruct cells: 0.013 to 0.176 (Dream-I MBPP uniform); LLaDA-I
  GSM8K uniform is negative (-0.003). E2 intervals condition on the fitted calibrators.
  Backup: full table with intervals, all-arm curves.}
\end{frame}

% ================================================================ 10 C1 results: every arm, and what the decoder commits
\begin{frame}{C1 results: with a decoder choosing, overconfidence grows with the contest}
  \framesubtitle{Gap $\Delta(m)$ against group size $m$ for each model; right: the tokens a decoder commits}
  \centering
  \COneFigure{c1_overview}{45mm}
  \par\vspace{1mm}
  \begin{takeaway}[fontupper=\footnotesize]
    With a decoder choosing, E1 is positive and claimed for all models. For tokens committed
    while many blanks remain, overconfidence is multiple times the ECE measured on random
    blanks, across every model
  \end{takeaway}
  \note{Blue: uniform states; orange: the states the top-k decoder visits. Dotted line: the arm's ECE
  over random masks, the usual calibration number. In decoder states Delta rises with m in every arm, so a
  token that won a field of 32 is more overconfident than a random masked position: E1 claimed in all seven
  decoder cells. In uniform states the sign varies. Y scales differ: base and 110M stay below 0.02, instruct
  reach 0.3. Right panel: c - a over the tokens the decoder actually commits, with 32-63 positions still masked,
  is 1.8 to 4.4 times the random-mask ECE in every arm, its interval above it; the instruct models reach 0.15
  to 0.27 with 128-255 masked. The mask count mixes field size with lost context, so this panel describes and
  does not test anything. Main-arm detail and the mechanism split: backup.}
\end{frame}

% ================================================================ 12 C1 results: E3
\begin{frame}{C1 results: blanks a decoder leaves are right less often (E3)}
  \framesubtitle{Blanks a decoder leaves against random blanks with as many masks, at equal confidence}
  \vspace{0.5mm}
  \centering
  \COneFigure{c1_e3_\SetupCOneMainArm}{30mm}\par
  \vspace{1mm}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.58\textwidth}
      \footnotesize\raggedright
      \lbl{Right panel.} Accuracy drop at equal confidence. \SetupCOneMainArmName{}: the accuracy
      drop is statistically significant ($p<0.001$). The decoder is fed the true tokens,
      confirming this drop stems from which blanks remain rather than decoder errors.
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.38\textwidth}
      \begin{takeaway}[fontupper=\footnotesize]
        Positive in every model and step size ($p\le0.002$): small for base models,
        much larger for instruction-tuned models. A calibration curve fitted on random blanks
        systematically overstates accuracy during decoding.
      \end{takeaway}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  \note{H3: yes. Against uniform states matched to the decoder's mask counts, the type effect is positive with
  its interval excluding 0 in all 21 rows (7 arms, k = 2, 4, 8), sup-t p at most 0.002. Small for the base and
  110M models (0.001 to 0.006), 0.03 to 0.06 for the instruct models. Against the plain uniform grid the
  interval holds 0 for LLaDA Base at k = 2 and 4. Teacher-forced, so it is about which positions are left
  masked, not about the decoder's own errors. So a calibration curve fitted on random masks of the same mask
  rate overstates accuracy in decoder states by about this much; C3a's calibrator is fitted on decoder states.
  E3 is exploratory and says nothing yet about decoding quality: that is the C3 comparison. Every arm: backup.}
\end{frame}

        & \CTEight{TEight\SetupCOneMainArm PositionETwoDecTopkConfKFour}{}
        & \CTEight{TEight\SetupCOneMainArm TokenTypeETwoDecTopkConfKFour}{} \\
      \bottomrule
    \end{tabular}}\par\vspace{2mm}
    \raggedright\footnotesize
    \lbl{Reduced against full precision} (test half of the documents): E1 differences across
    states are reported in the table.\par
  \else
    \Pend{42mm}{}{Waits for \texttt{paper/tables/c1/macros\_c1.tex}, written by
      \texttt{scripts/c1\_paper\_outputs.py} from \texttt{results/t8/<Label>/ablation.json}
      (\texttt{scripts/run\_controls.py}).}{Main arm: E1 and E2 without the control, then with position,
      token type and (E1 only) a temperature per mask-rate bin, in uniform and decoder states; below it,
      the 4-bit against fp16 change of E1. All arms: backup.}\par
  \fi
  \vspace{1.2mm}
  \begin{takeaway}[fontupper=\footnotesize]
    \textbf{Result.} With a decoder choosing, E1 stays positive under every control across all models
    (largest change under temperature rescaling). LLaDA Base's small E1 on random
    blanks vanishes once token type is controlled, demonstrating the core effect's robustness.
    $^{\ddagger}$: adding the control significantly changes the value; most do, by small amounts.
  \end{takeaway}
  \note{A column close to plain: the control did not matter. Decoder-state E1 keeps its sign under position,
  token type and a temperature per mask-rate bin in all seven arms; the largest move is LLaDA-I MBPP with a
  temperature, 0.156 to 0.125. So the growth is not where winners sit, what kind of token they are, or an
  overall over- or underconfidence one temperature per mask rate could fix. Uniform-state E1 of the base and
  110M models moves by up to 0.004, the size of those effects, so there the controls matter: token type takes
  LLaDA Base's claimed uniform E1 to 0.0002 [-0.0010, 0.0014]. 4-bit against fp16: both intervals hold 0, but
  in decoder states the difference (0.0055) is as large as that cell's E1 (0.006), and fp16 E1 on that report half
  is itself about 0 (0.0003), so a precision effect is not ruled out. Decoder-state E2 changes by
  -0.0025 [-0.0030, -0.0021], the size of the base models' E2. Exploratory: no Holm family. Every arm: backup. E2 here uses logistic calibrators for both curves, as in
  Table 4, so its plain value differs from slide 8's.}
\end{frame}

% ================================================================ 11 C2 probe
\begin{frame}{C2: a synthetic task where we know the true answer distribution}
  \framesubtitle{Our 110M model, fine-tuned on it, so (A) and (B) can be computed exactly at every step}
  \vspace{1mm}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.5\textwidth}
      \begin{itemize}\footnotesize
        \item \textbf{Task}: fill in the values of JSON records built from real
              schemas (SchemaStore), multiple fields each, one token per value.
        \item \textbf{Link strength $\rho$}: fields come in pairs. With probability $\rho$, written
              at the start of the record, the second field (follower) is fixed by the first
              (leader); otherwise it is drawn independently. So we know $p^{*}$ exactly.
        \item \textbf{Model}: our 110M model, fine-tuned and tested across multiple $\rho$ settings.
        \item \textbf{Decoding}: all values start blank; each step a rule picks $k$ fields, the most
              confident or at random, and we fill them with the true values.
        \item \textbf{Check}: \A + \B equals the directly computed total error within numerical tolerance.
      \end{itemize}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.46\textwidth}
      \vspace{1mm}
      % instance text: artifacts/probe/eval_instances.jsonl, schema "tsd", rho = 1; values masked
      \begin{panel}[colback=plane, colframe=plane]
        {\color{ink2}\scriptsize one test record ($\rho = 1$), values blank}\par\vspace{1mm}
        \ttfamily\scriptsize
        \{{\color{accentdark}"\_rho":"1.00"},\\
        \hspace*{2mm}"bundle":{\color{muted}[M]}, "path":{\color{muted}[M]},\\
        \hspace*{2mm}"ref":{\color{muted}[M]}, "repo":{\color{muted}[M]},\\
        \hspace*{2mm}"stats":{\color{muted}[M]}, "version":{\color{muted}[M]}\}
      \end{panel}
      \vspace{1.5mm}
      \begin{panel}
        \paneltitle{Per step, for the committed set $S$}
        \A $= \sum_{i\in S} H(p^{*}_i) - H(p^{*}_S)$: zero unless a leader and its follower
        are committed together.\par\vspace{0.6mm}
        \B $= \sum_{i\in S}\mathrm{KL}(p^{*}_i \,\|\, p_{\theta,i})$: each field's own error,
        including probability put on impossible values.\par\vspace{0.6mm}
        Summed over steps, per field, with bootstrap intervals over records.
      \end{panel}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  % rho grid {0, .25, .5, .75, 1}: artifacts/probe/spec.json (rhos); k {1, 2, 4, 8}: T9 grid.
\end{frame}

% ================================================================ 12 C2 crossover
\begin{frame}{C2: dependency errors \A dominate only with strong links and large steps}
  \vspace{0.5mm}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.53\textwidth}
      \centering\includegraphics[height=58mm]{c2_crossover_ft110m-v3-visible}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.45\textwidth}
      \vspace{1mm}
      \begin{itemize}\footnotesize
        \item \A is negligible at step size 1 or without link strength ($\rho = 0$), and grows with both.
        \item For strong links, \A overtakes \B as step size increases; picking by confidence causes this crossover at smaller step sizes.
        \item For weak links, estimation error \B remains larger across step sizes.
      \end{itemize}
      \vspace{1.5mm}
      \begin{panel}[colback=wash, colframe=wash]
        \paneltitle{Strong links ($\rho = 1$), large steps, confidence top-$k$}
        Dependency error \A accounts for the vast majority of total error, far exceeding estimation error \B.
      \end{panel}
      % \src{Main model: the fine-tune that never saw the $\rho$ marker masked (backup).
      % \CTwoProbeNBoot{} bootstrap resamples.}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}

% ================================================================ 13 C2 corrections
\begin{frame}{C2: three findings that correct our plan}
  \vspace{1mm}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.5\textwidth}
      \begin{panel}[fontupper=\scriptsize, before skip=0pt, after skip=1.2mm]
        \paneltitle{1 · Picking by confidence raises \A, not \B}
        {\color{muted}Expected: picking the surest fields would raise \B.}\par
        Where \B is compared, intervals overlap; \A rises substantially compared
        to random selection.
      \end{panel}
      \begin{panel}[fontupper=\scriptsize, before skip=0pt, after skip=1.2mm]
        \paneltitle{2 · \B also depends on $\rho$}
        {\color{muted}Expected: $\rho$ changes only \A.}\par
        Even at step size 1, \B increases with link strength $\rho$: the model only partly uses the $\rho$ marker.
      \end{panel}
      \begin{panel}[fontupper=\scriptsize, before skip=0pt, after skip=1.2mm]
        \paneltitle{3 · \A and \B trade off as $k$ grows}
        With strong links, as step size grows, \B decreases while \A increases: error from co-committed tokens shifts into \A.
      \end{panel}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.47\textwidth}
      \centering\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]{c2_untuned_vs_tuned}\par
      \vspace{1mm}\raggedright
      \begin{itemize}\footnotesize
        \item Without fine-tuning, estimation error \B dominates everywhere, with \A remaining a minor fraction of the total.
        \item Picking by confidence fills a leader and its follower in the same step more
              often than chance, so \A overtakes \B at smaller $k$.
      \end{itemize}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

% ================================================================ 15 C3: the rule and its calibrator
\begin{frame}{C3a: let corrected confidence decide how many tokens to commit}
  \framesubtitle{Uses only numbers the decoder already computes, so no extra model calls}
  \vspace{0.5mm}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.5\textwidth}
      \begin{itemize}\footnotesize
        \item \textbf{Order}: rank the blanks of the current block by the model's own score
              $\ell$, as top-$k$ does.
        \item \textbf{Count}: commit the top $n$, where $n$ is the number of blanks whose
              corrected confidence $\hat c \ge 1-\alpha$ (at least one).
        \item \textbf{Corrector}: a small logistic model that also sees the median score, the
              share still masked and the number of blanks.
        \item \textbf{Fit once, then frozen}: on the fit halves of LLaDA-8B-Instruct runs on
              GSM8K and MBPP ($k = 2, 4, 8$ pooled); test halves never used.
        \item \textbf{Known shift}: real decoding starts from 256 blanks, while fit states sat
              inside a reference answer; we count steps outside the fit range.
      \end{itemize}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.47\textwidth}
      \ifCThreeMacros
        {\begin{panel}\paneltitle{Corrector (T11)}
          {\footnotesize\setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt}\arrayrulecolor{base}
          \begin{tabular}{@{}l r r@{}}
            & {\color{ink2}GSM8K} & {\color{ink2}MBPP} \\ \midrule
            fit documents & \Cres{CThreeTElevenGsmFitDocs} & \Cres{CThreeTElevenMbppFitDocs} \\
            ECE, raw $\sigma(\ell)$ & \Cres{CThreeTElevenGsmReportECERaw} & \Cres{CThreeTElevenMbppReportECERaw} \\
            ECE, corrected $\hat c$ & \Cres{CThreeTElevenGsmReportECECal} & \Cres{CThreeTElevenMbppReportECECal} \\
            states where $\hat c$ rises with $\ell$ & \Cres{CThreeTElevenGsmMonotoneShare} & \Cres{CThreeTElevenMbppMonotoneShare} \\
            decode steps outside fit range & \Cres{CThreeTTwelveGsmOutsideShare} & \Cres{CThreeTTwelveMbppOutsideShare} \\
          \end{tabular}}\par\vspace{1mm}
          {\scriptsize\color{ink2}ECE on held-out report-half states (teacher-forced), as in \S6.}
        \end{panel}}% braces, not a group: an \else straight after \end{panel} upsets TeX
      \else
        \Pend{40mm}{}{Waits for the frozen calibrators in \texttt{artifacts/c3/}
          (\texttt{scripts/fit\_c3a\_calibrator.py}) and a macros file for their diagnostics.}{%
          \begin{stubs}\scriptsize
            \item Development check: calibration error of $\hat c$ against raw $\sigma(\ell)$ on
                  held-out fit-half documents (not a headline).
            \item Share of decode steps outside the fit range, per task.
            \item Share of fit states where $\hat c$ never decreases with $\ell$.
          \end{stubs}}
      \fi
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  \note{The calibrators are fitted on the fit half only and frozen in artifacts/c3/. On held-out
  report-half states (teacher-forced) they cut the ECE of the commit confidence from 0.060 to 0.004 (GSM8K)
  and 0.040 to 0.005 (MBPP), and c-hat never decreases with l in any fit state, so C3a's commits keep the
  calibrated-error guarantee there. The last row comes from the T12 run: how often free-running states
  fall outside what the calibrator saw.}
\end{frame}

% ================================================================ 16 C3: matched-speed comparison
\begin{frame}{C3: is the corrected rule more accurate at the same speed?}
  \framesubtitle{LLaDA-8B-Instruct answers GSM8K and MBPP test problems itself}
  \vspace{0.5mm}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.58\textwidth}
      \CThreeFigure{t12_matched_speed}{50mm}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.395\textwidth}
      \footnotesize\raggedright
      \lbl{Decoders.} Top-$k$, Fast-dLLM threshold, entropy-bounded, margin, KLASS, PC-Sampler,
      and C3a, each at three speeds.\par\vspace{1mm}
      \lbl{Reading.} Up and to the right is better. Speed is tokens per step, so compare
      accuracy at the same $x$.\par\vspace{1mm}
      \lbl{Claim.} A gain needs higher accuracy at the same speed, beyond the
      intervals.\par\vspace{1.5mm}
      \begin{takeaway}[fontupper=\footnotesize]
        \textbf{Answer:} \CThreeAnswer
      \end{takeaway}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  \note{GSM8K, all 659 report-half problems, 21 settings. At about 4 tokens per step, C3a minus decoder,
  paired over problems: threshold -0.002 [-0.014, 0.012], entropy-bounded -0.005 [-0.035, 0.026], top-k
  +0.059, margin +0.053, PC-Sampler +0.082 (all three intervals above 0). So C3a is indistinguishable from the raw
  threshold rule and beats the fixed-count decoders, as the raw threshold does; calibration makes alpha
  a per-token error target but adds no accuracy. At 8 tokens per step the raw threshold is ahead (0.674 against 0.610). KLASS's two faster
  rows are off its published operating point (tau lowered to 0.2-0.29, reaching 3.9-4.9 tokens per
  step; KL history kept per 32-token block), so no comparison rests on them. Settings: chat prompt, greedy, one seed, fp16,
  one H200. MBPP (121 of 250 problems; budget limit): C3a at 3.61
  tokens per step, pass@1 0.355; minus threshold 0.000 [-0.033, 0.033], minus entropy-bounded 0.000
  [-0.058, 0.058]. Top-k, margin and PC-Sampler ran at 4.00, 10.9 percent faster than C3a, outside the
  +-10 percent matching rule, so they are not compared there.
  Sanity check and cost: backup.}
\end{frame}

% ================================================================ 17 limitations
\begin{frame}{What we got wrong, and the limits of these results}
  \vspace{1mm}
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.485\textwidth}
      \begin{panel}[height=60mm]
        \paneltitle{Claims we checked}
        \begin{itemize}\scriptsize
          \item Unequal noise across blanks alone makes winners overconfident (initial premise):
                false, Proposition 1.
          \item Picking by confidence inflates \B: on the synthetic
                task it raises \A instead.
          \item $\rho$ changes only \A: \B rises with $\rho$ too.
          \item Real-text C2 as exact measurements: they are proxies that give a
                direction but no split in nats.
        \end{itemize}
      \end{panel}
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.485\textwidth}
      \begin{panel}[height=60mm]
        \paneltitle{Limits}
        \begin{itemize}\scriptsize
          \item C2's exact values hold for one synthetic task and one 110M model.
          \item Neither fine-tuned model passed our check that it reads the $\rho$ marker; we use
                the one with lower validation loss (the other: backup).
          \item The disagreement proxy follows \A weakly, and mostly through $k$.
          \item C1 is teacher-forced (the decoder sees the true tokens); E2 intervals treat
                the fitted calibration curves as fixed.
          \item C3: one model, greedy decoding, one seed
        \end{itemize}
      \end{panel}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Backup: proofs}
  \framesubtitle{$W_i$: the event that $i \in P$ wins, $i = \arg\max_{j\in P}\ell_j$; ties broken by independent randomness $U$}
  \vspace{1.5mm}
  \footnotesize
  \begin{columns}[T,onlytextwidth]
    \begin{column}{0.485\textwidth}\raggedright
      \paneltitle{Proposition 1}
      Suppose, given $s$, each pair $(\ell_i, a_i)$ is independent of
      $\ell_{-i} = (\ell_j)_{j \in M,\, j \neq i}$. Let $Z = (\ell_i, s)$ and
      $Y = (\ell_{-i}, P, U)$.\par\vspace{1mm}
      Given $s$, $(\ell_i, a_i) \perp \ell_{-i}$ and $(P, U) \perp (\ell_j, a_j)_{j\in M}$, so
      $(\ell_i, a_i) \perp Y \mid s$, and by weak union $a_i \perp Y \mid Z$, i.e.\
      $\mathbb{E}[a_i \mid Y, Z] = \pi(\ell_i, s)$.\par\vspace{1mm}
      $W_i$ is determined by $(Y, Z)$, so for every bounded measurable $h$
      \[
        \mathbb{E}[a_i h(Z) \mathbb{1}_{W_i}] = \mathbb{E}[\pi(\ell_i, s) h(Z) \mathbb{1}_{W_i}].
      \]
      Dividing by $\Pr(W_i) > 0$ gives $\mathbb{E}[a_i \mid Z, W_i] = \pi(\ell_i, s)$ a.s.
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.485\textwidth}\raggedright
      \paneltitle{Proposition 2}
      Exactly one $W_i$ holds. Applying the display with $h \equiv 1$, summing over $i$ and
      averaging over $s$:
      \[
        \mathbb{E}_m[a] = \textstyle\sum_i \mathbb{E}_m[a_i \mathbb{1}_{W_i}]
        = \textstyle\sum_i \mathbb{E}_m[\pi(\ell_i, s)\mathbb{1}_{W_i}]
        = \mathbb{E}_m[\pi(\ell, s)],
      \]
      so $\Delta(m) = \mathbb{E}_m[\sigma(\ell) - \pi(\ell, s)]$; add and subtract
      $\pi(\ell)$.\par\vspace{1mm}
      At $m = 1$, $\mathbb{E}_1[\pi(\ell)] = \mathbb{E}_1[a]$ by the tower property and
      $\mathbb{E}_1[\pi(\ell, s)] = \mathbb{E}_1[a]$ by the display, so the field term is 0.
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
\end{frame}

  \begin{itemize}\footnotesize
    \item At rate 1 every input is the same all-\texttt{[MASK]} sequence. That one state gives
          the 110M model nearly all of its disagreement (\CTwoTTenDisAllRatesKEight{} at $k = 8$
          over all ten rates); LLaDA does not disagree there. The main slide reads rates
          0.1–0.9.
    \item Documents under 256 tokens are skipped; at least
          \CTwoTTenMinMasked{} masked positions per state; \CTwoTTenNBoot{} document-bootstrap
          resamples.
  \end{itemize}
\end{frame}

  \vspace{0.5mm}

    \begin{column}{0.575\textwidth}
      \ifCOneMacros
        {\footnotesize\setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt}\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.18}

          & \multicolumn{2}{c}{$\beta_z$, no state effects} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{$\beta_z$, state effects} \\
          \cmidrule(lr){2-3}\cmidrule(lr){4-5}
          {\color{ink2}Arm} & {\color{ink2}uniform} & {\color{ink2}decoder} & {\color{ink2}uniform} & {\color{ink2}decoder} \\
          \midrule
          \CBetaRow{LLaDA Base}{LladaBase}
          \CBetaRow{Dream Base}{DreamBase}
          \CBetaRow{LLaDA-I GSM8K}{LladaInstructGsm}
          \CBetaRow{LLaDA-I MBPP}{LladaInstructMbpp}
          \CBetaRow{Dream-I GSM8K}{DreamInstructGsm}
          \CBetaRow{Dream-I MBPP}{DreamInstructMbpp}
          \CBetaRow{MDLM-110M}{Mdlm}
          \bottomrule
        \end{tabular}}% braces, not a group: an \else straight after a tabular upsets TeX
      \else
        \Pend{52mm}{}{Waits for \texttt{paper/tables/c1/macros\_c1.tex}, written by
          \texttt{scripts/c1\_paper\_outputs.py} from \texttt{results/c1/<Label>/results.json}
          (\texttt{regression.eq2\_nofe}, \texttt{eq2\_fe}).}{$\beta_z$ without and with state effects, one
          row per arm, uniform and decoder ($k{=}4$) states. Point estimates; intervals: backup.}
      \fi
    \end{column}
    \begin{column}{0.395\textwidth}
      \footnotesize\raggedright
      \lbl{Field effect.} $\beta_z<0$ without state effects and $\approx 0$ with them; it
      should agree with a positive E2.\par\vspace{1mm}
      \lbl{Shared errors.} $\beta_z\neq 0$ with state effects: positions of a state are wrong
      together, Proposition 1 fails, and E2 is not a field effect.\par\vspace{1mm}
      \lbl{Caution.} In T0, shared errors gave a \emph{positive} $\beta_z$ without state effects and
      a negative field term, so we read $\beta_z$ only beside the sign of E2.\par\vspace{1.5mm}
      \begin{takeaway}[fontupper=\footnotesize]
        \textbf{Reading.} No state effects: excludes 0 in 14 of 14, negative in 12. With
        them: holds 0 in 8 of those 12. A field effect, small where E2 is. Diagnostic only.
      \end{takeaway}
    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  \note{Reading (a) of four: negative without state effects, about zero with them, E2 positive, so a field
  effect. Without FE the interval excludes 0 in all 14 cells and is negative in 12; with FE it holds 0 in 8 of those 12 (E2 positive in all 8 but LLaDA-I GSM8K uniform). The other 4
  negative cells (LLaDA Base uniform, Dream Base decoder, LLaDA-I MBPP uniform, Dream-I GSM8K decoder) exclude 0
  with FE as well: shared errors there.
  The two positive cells, LLaDA Base and MDLM-110M decoder states, have E2 near the estimator's T0 bias; the
  110M one has a negative E2 beside its positive beta_z, the pattern T0's shared-error world gave, at small size. Intervals: backup table. If asked about gamma (Eq. 3, the lower-ranked pool members):
  Holm, run within each arm and kind of state, rejects 24 of the 42 tests of gamma_2-4, in 8 of the 14 rows, all positive, all in the instruct models and Dream Base decoder
  states: at equal confidence lower-ranked members are right more often than the winner, which Proposition 1
  excludes when its conditions hold. We read it, like the within-state ICC (above 0 in every arm), as a sign
  of shared errors or of a calibration slope that varies by state. None of it is a claim.}
\end{frame}

    \begin{column}{0.48\textwidth}
      \footnotesize\raggedright
      \lbl{Right.} Below the diagonal: confidence exceeds accuracy. ECE sees only this picture,

    \end{column}
  \end{columns}
  \note{LLaDA-8B-Base: in uniform states Delta(m) falls slightly with m (E1 small, negative); in decoder
  states it rises (E1 positive). The dashed field terms stay near zero in both, so the change is mostly own
  miscalibration and we do not read it as a winner's curse; decoder states also carry a shared-error term
  of -0.008 [-0.009, -0.006] at m = 32, and the independent estimator does not identify their field term. Estimator reads the field term slightly high in T0, so a small
  positive E2 is weaker than its interval suggests. Other arms: backup.}
\end{frame}

  \begin{takeaway}[fontupper=\footnotesize]
    \ifcsname CThreeTTwelveSanityTopKAcc\endcsname
      \textbf{Reading.} Both published accuracies lie inside our 95\% intervals (top-$k$
      \Cres{CThreeTTwelveSanityTopKAcc} against 0.793, threshold \Cres{CThreeTTwelveSanityThresholdAcc}
      against 0.792), though our points are higher. A decoder faster in steps but not in seconds
      is reported as such.
    \else
      \textbf{How to read.} If the sanity row misses the published numbers, nothing after it is
      comparable and we say that first. A faster decoder in steps that is not faster in seconds is
      reported as such.
    \fi
  \end{takeaway}
  \note{Sanity (plan item 4): 200 fit-half GSM8K problems at Fast-dLLM's settings, 5-shot. Top-k 0.835
  [0.777, 0.880] against a published 0.793; threshold 0.845 [0.788, 0.889] against 0.792 (Wilson
  intervals). Both published values are inside, but our points are 4 to 5 points higher, beyond the
  plan's 1-2 point bar; 200 problems give intervals about 10 points wide. The T12 report run used
  one H200 per task (sanity run on RTX 2080 Ti); MBPP stopped at 121 of 250 problems when compute budget ran out.}
\end{frame}
